questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the university surrounded by nature, and that there are many options to do outdoor activities like hiking, skiing and surfing. I also liked that the main language was english.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I would say it was relatively easy to find information, and people were very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I would have preferred they there were more introduction days in the beginning of the exchange to be able to meet people. There was only one day (imagine day), which was a bit stressful, and its a bit harder to get to know people in classes.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Everyone on exchange lived in Walter Gage or Fairview Crescent. These are shared apartments, where you live with 4-6 people, usually other exchange students.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There are meal plan options, but both Walter gage and Fairview Crescent are shared apartments, where there is a kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is a bit difficult to get housing on campus, and only 50% of exchange students got campus housing. Also you receive information about whether or not you got campus housing very late (in june if you are attending UBC in the fall). If they didn't get campus housing, people got housing through facebook marketplace, airbnb or craigslist.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a bit confusing to register for classes, and understand the different faculties at the university. Furthermore, as an exchange student you have to rank 10 classes that you would like, and understanding the timetable and choosing the classes is a bit difficult.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't know, because I didn't need help during the application process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I wanted some more creative classes, and those where a bit difficult to get, since students in those faculties have priority in those classes. The creative writing faculty is easier to get classes in.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you dont get the classes you wanted in the first place, there is an option to change classes during the first two weeks of school. You can also talk to professors if there isn't space in their classes, since there might still be options to join the class.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had 200 and 300 courses. I am on my third year of studying, so these courses fit relatively well. I would say 200 courses are easier than the courses I would have had in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching at UBC is very different to UCPH. At UCPH you are more independant and you are only graded for the final exam. At UBC the assignments, quizzes and your attendance during the term are a part of your grade, and you have to do these to pass the courses. This was a bit stressful for me to get used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
CRWR 203 Introduction to Writing for Children and Young Adults
GEOG 210 Vancouver and Its Region
GEOG 312 Climate Change: Science and Society
GEOS 207 Introduction to Biogeography

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked the creative writing course I had, because it was different to any course I had before, and the teacher was very nice.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There is an obligatory health insurance from UBC which is around 1800 DKK in total. There is also an obligatory travel pass which is around 850 DKK for four months.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going out to eat is less expensive then in Denmark, but grocery shopping is very expensive in Canada (more than in Denmark). In general Canada is pretty expensive to stay in, especially if you take part in many outdoor activities. If you like skiing it is possible to buy a student season pass for Whistler for around 3500 DKK, but they get sold out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are many available. There is a buddy program for exchange students where you can meet people. There is also an outdoor club, surf club, ski club, running club and so on. There are club days where it is possible to learn about the clubs. The clubs also arrange trips.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking, surfing (in tofino), skiing, rock climbing. The mountains are very close and it is possible to rent cars from turo or evo to go to the different places.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
If you like hiking there are many cute huts on top of mountains you can overnight in. For example by elfin lakes. If you go in september/october there might be bears (i saw seven on this hike), so remember to bring bear spray. There is also brew hut, which is a hut owned by the outdoor club. 
There is a rock climbing trip with the outdoor club in one of the weekends in september. Another weekend there is a surftrip with the surfclub. For the opening weekend of whistler there is a ski trip.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is not that different to Denmark, and everyone was very friendly and spoke english, so relatively easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go on some of the trips with the clubs, and get put in a random car. You will most likely be placed with locals since they have cars. I met some nice local people on the surf trip by doing this. Otherwise having classes with group activities or field trips.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any, they are just a lot more friendly in public than danish people. They drink less alcohol, and all bars close at 2pm.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness and openness to doing outdoor activities.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Save up a lot of money, because it is expensive.
- Think about bringing a sleeping bag and sleeping mat if you like outdoor activities (you can also buy it there, but if you already have everything).
- It is a beautiful place, with so many options to do things, so go to the mountains and hike and swim in a glacial lake <33

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is a very big school, with a lot of exchange students. We were about 25 people from UCPH, and in total around 45 danish people (from other universities like CBS and DTU).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people and the insane nature being so close. Being able to go somewhere completly on my own, and having a great time.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It feels lonely sometimes, especially in the beginning, because none of your saftey people are there, but everyone feels this way.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
